summary: A 1933 report describes a 100-ft steel tower being erected by CCC camp Alabax P-62; no source found for completion, staffing, fate or the site today.

events.note: Steel tower reported as being erected by CCC camp Alabax P-62 on the old Baxley-Hazelhurst road. The report describes work in progress, not a finished tower.

evidence.supports: 1933 Macon Telegraph item: steel tower 100 feet high being erected on the old Baxley-Hazelhurst road by CCC camp Alabax P-62
evidence.quote: A steel tower 100 feet high is being erected on the old Baxley-Hazelhurst road by CCC camp Alabax P-62

evidence.supports: Tower to be connected by telephone to Camp Alabax at Baxley so fires could be reported
evidence.quote: will be connected by telephone to Camp Alabax at Baxley to notify of any forest fire as soon as discovered

evidence.supports: Tower was supposed to cover a twelve-mile radius
evidence.quote: It is supposed to cover a twelve-mile radius.

evidence.supports: tnlandforms list: baxley in Appling County, elevation 196, codes BLL-64701 and gfc-801
Forest Lookouts Baxley page places the Baxley tower in Appling County

sources.title: Baxley - Forest Lookouts (quoting The Macon Telegraph, December 3, 1933)

notes_for_editor: The only 1933 evidence is one newspaper item quoted on a lookout-history site; the camp name is printed as 'Alabax P-62' and is reproduced as such. Whether the tnlandforms 'baxley' entry is the same tower is unverified: both lists use the name Baxley for an Appling County site, and the story says so. facts.height_m 30.5 converts the 1933 plan figure of 100 ft and is not a measured height. Two WebSearch passes (Appling County tower, CCC Alabax) found nothing further. Suggest the Georgia Forestry Commission Appling County unit or the Georgia Archives for completion and later history.
